Uncloud v0.4.38 brings the same Chisel and engine fixes to Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon and Linux x64. The three installers and signed updates are published together from one source revision.

- Chisel approvals appear inside the app window and in Notifications, with the proposed command, file path and full details available before approval. Permission requests and follow-up questions share the same response state, so an answered request cannot be submitted again from another view.
- Compatible local GGUF, MLX and MLX vision runtimes use native function calls and real tool-result turns. Code and braces are preserved when tasks are resumed. Ordinary Chat adds no identity correction, date or persona instructions.
- Chisel retains completed steps, observes failures and validates completion. Longer workflows have a bounded 40-action allowance instead of stopping after a few observations. Cancellation and command timeouts stop the process tree.
- A governed document tool creates and reads back actual PDF, Word and Excel files. It checks the output format before replacing an existing file; failed output leaves the original intact. File, Python and shell actions use the selected workspace and engine environment.
- Chat now accepts text-based PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, CSV, text and source files without requiring a vision model. The picker no longer hides readable files by extension. Extraction runs locally, one bad file does not abort a whole selection, and requests rejected before an answer return their files and question to the composer for retry. Each file is limited to 10 MB; long extracts are labelled as excerpts. Scanned PDFs require OCR and encrypted PDFs require an unlocked copy.
- macOS GGUF runtime installation uses a verified compiler-free package. Runtime probing recognizes Metal devices and does not remember a temporary probe failure as permanent CPU-only capability. Windows CPU and Vulkan launch handling, context validation before model replacement, and GGUF quantization validation are also repaired.
- The model picker remains available after a completed or failed Chisel run. Tool output is displayed as plain text, and native model replies retain Markdown formatting. High-quality Piper voices remain optional.

Verification before packaging: 1,296 backend tests passed (12 optional tests skipped), all 242 frontend tests passed, and the frontend and macOS production builds passed. Live GGUF tests on Apple Silicon verified file creation, editing, reading, listing and command execution, plus real PDF, Word and Excel creation and read-back. The original input and final document hashes were unchanged during the read-only check. A rendered PDF was visually inspected. Chat upload tests cover real PDF, Word, Excel and PowerPoint documents, text encodings, corrupt/encrypted/empty files, size and excerpt limits, authentication, mixed selections and retry preservation.

GitHub checks the source, dependency resolution and platform installers before publication. Physical Windows and Linux inference was not tested locally. Models can still choose unsuitable actions or generate invalid custom code; permission policies and bounded execution remain in force. No generation-speed increase is claimed.
